_consumes_is_narrower_than_the_reference: StegVerse-org also consumes stegverse.canonical-state-transition-receipt/v1. This organization runs no canonical state transition emitter, so admitting that schema would declare an intake nothing here produces. It is added when such an emitter exists, not before.
_what_propagation_means_here: Organization receipts are recorded at the organization level and then batched to master-records. Those are two acts. Recording is real under ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_LOCK the moment it is appended; batching hands a segment this organization has independently verified and released to the recorder for durable custody. The release predecessor is a VERIFIED_ORGANIZATION_RECEIPT_CHAIN_SEGMENT, where verified means each receipt was re-digested against its own body before the batch digest was taken.
_what_the_recorder_is_not: master-records holds custody, reconstruction and cross-organization history, and holds no transition authority. It is not this organization's runtime-reality authority and may not gate it: an organization transition is real when it is appended under the organization ledger lock, not when a batch carrying it is recorded downstream. A batch that has not been released or recorded is a value in the attempted transition's evidence state, not a blocker and not proof of non-occurrence.
_why_the_submission_refuses_today: The federation directory's row for master-records declares org_control_service master-records.org-control and no addressed_service. A control service is the control plane, not a custody ledger, and submitting a batch to it because it is the service that happens to exist is the identity-addressing substitution this boundary refuses everywhere else. So the submission refuses immediately with a named predicate and the release stands. Nothing is queued against the day the service is declared, nothing polls for it, and no machine is awaited. Registered as SGHOST-EXEMPTION-006.
_previous_state: This field read null, on the ground that naming a propagation target with no submitter behind it would be a declared capability with nothing enforcing it. The release surface now exists, so the target is named and what is still absent -- the peer's declared custody service -- is named separately rather than hidden behind a null target.
